currentContext.strengths: Network of 1000+ connected operators allowing SMS termination in any part of the world with the best routing; 280+ direct MNO connects and 900+ MNO connections across the Proximus Global combine|Full-stack omnichannel CPaaS platform bringing messaging, voice, email and emerging digital channels into a single integrated ecosystem, so enterprises manage customer journeys through one integration|Carrier-grade, resilient global infrastructure with 20+ global data centers delivering APIs at enterprise scale|Membership of Proximus Global alongside BICS and Telesign, adding global carrier connectivity, digital identity and fraud prevention, and enabling cross-selling across Europe and North America|Route Mobile serves as the innovation engine for Proximus Global, with innovations built by its teams deployed across global markets|Scale and stickiness of enterprise relationships: 3,100+ clients served and 174.9 Bn billable transactions processed in FY 2025-26|Security and compliance embedded across the platform through stringent governance and global compliance standards, plus regulatory expertise across jurisdictions
currentContext.strategies: Expand the AI-first platform and embed AI across the customer engagement stack, using best available AI technologies rather than building foundational models in-house|Deepen leadership in Network APIs and Digital Identity, scaling the Konera Network API Platform after transitioning it from experimentation to execution with integrations from major operators|Accelerate innovation across omnichannel customer engagement and grow enterprise presence across India and international markets|Improve operating efficiency and sustain profitable growth through disciplined execution|Use India as the innovation engine: engineering teams design, develop and validate products in India for deployment across international markets, supported by a new technology hub in Hyderabad for AI, product engineering and Network APIs|Run the Konera Strategic Expansion Plan out of India, where new capabilities are developed, pressure-tested with customers and cybersecurity partners, and refined before wider global deployment|Leverage the Proximus Global combination with BICS and Telesign to cross-sell and expand reach across Europe, North America and other strategic markets|The Company maintains a board-adopted Dividend Distribution Policy alongside its other corporate policies (published on the Company website), and the Board has placed a dividend on equity shares for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 before members for approval as ordinary business at the 22nd AGM. Governance framework: a six-member Board as on March 31, 2026 with one Executive Director/MD and five Non-Executive Directors including three Independent Directors, a Non-Executive and Non-Independent Chairman with the roles of Chairman, MD and CEO held by different individuals, and Board committees covering audit and internal controls, financial reporting, risk management, nomination and remuneration and CSR. All related party transactions are conducted under Audit Committee scrutiny on an arm's-length basis in the ordinary course of business, and the Company reports no material unlisted Indian subsidiaries during FY 2025-26. Statutory auditors M S K A & Associates LLP have been recommended for appointment for five years in place of the retiring auditors; the FY 2025-26 Auditors' Report and the Secretarial Audit Report carry no qualifications, reservations or adverse remarks, and there was no modified audit opinion.|Scope 2 emissions of 171.37 metric tons of CO2 equivalent in the year, a total reduction of 17.58 metric tons of CO2 versus the previous year, achieved through dedicated energy optimization including efficient HVAC systems and LED lighting across facilities|Water consumption of 3722.84 KL managed responsibly during the year|Waste initiatives eliminated single-use plastics and established comprehensive e-waste recycling programmes|Forward commitment to enhanced climate action through continued emissions reduction and renewable energy adoption, plus implementation of circular economy principles in operations|CSR investment of INR 2.36 crores in community programmes focused on healthcare, education and elder care, with the CSR Committee chaired by Independent Director Mrs. Harita Gupta|Certified quality management system complying with ISO 9001:2015 and information security management system complying with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (certified by KVQA Certification Services Private Limited); ISO/IEC 27001:2022 surveillance was conducted during the year|Board-level ESG oversight with 50% independent directors and zero tolerance for bribery and corruption; sustainability issues overseen through the Nomination & Remuneration, CSR and Risk Management Committees, with Managing Director Mr. Rajdipkumar Gupta the highest authority for the Business Responsibility policies|Risk management systems established across all markets include climate-related risks|The Company states it has set no specific ESG commitments, goals or targets with defined timelines, identifying only goals complementing its core business and its CSR programme in healthcare, education and sports|NGRBC policies cover eight of the nine principles (P7 public advocacy has no dedicated policy) and extend to value chain partners through the ESG policy, Anti-Fraud/Anti-Bribery & Anti-Corruption Policy, Supplier Code of Conduct, POSH policy, insider trading code and Data Protection Policy
currentContext.expansion: Route Mobile is an asset-light CPaaS business and the annual report describes expansion as platform build-out, capability addition and inorganic activity rather than physical capacity. Strategic Pillar 01 ('Elevating the platform') sets out broadening beyond traditional messaging into a full customer-engagement ecosystem: expanding omnichannel engagement across WhatsApp, RCS, voice and other digital channels through the OCEAN platform; embedding AI and GenAI into engagement workflows including conversational interfaces, enterprise integrations and intelligent automation; and developing Network API and firewall solutions that use telecom infrastructure for identity verification, fraud prevention and secure digital interactions. Pillar 02 ('Accelerating AI-led innovation') makes India the Group's innovation hub, where new capabilities are developed, tested and scaled for global deployment, including building GenAI-native engagement solutions across chat, voice and messaging, deploying AI across engineering, testing, customer support and operational workflows, and scaling India-built Network API innovations across the global Proximus ecosystem. Pillar 04 ('Driving growth through partnerships and M&A') covers evaluating acquisitions in conversational AI, chatbot technologies and adjacent CPaaS capabilities, partnerships for faster entry into priority geographies and industry segments, collaboration with ISVs, telecom operators and technology partners, and cross-selling across the Proximus Global portfolio including BICS and Telesign. Pillar 03 focuses on deepening relationships within a base of more than 3,100 enterprise customers. The BRSR states that R&D and capex investments in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts were 'None', as the nature of the business does not involve material carbon emission or other pollutant. No rupee capex quantum is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.
currentContext.mdna: Changing business composition moderated revenue alongside lower-margin international A2P SMS volumes, while profitability improved through product mix optimization, operational efficiencies and increasing contribution from higher-value solutions|Enterprise demand is shifting from app-based interactions toward autonomous resolution, with Agentic AI able to reason, decide and execute multi-step actions across systems - management sees the combination of intelligence, trust and seamless execution becoming a defining competitive advantage|AI capability expansion is expected to lift customer satisfaction: multilingual AI now supports more than 50 languages and intelligent flow detection reduces customer service resolution times by as much as 75%|Network API integrations on the Konera Platform created a new stack of enterprise solutions, unlocked new revenue streams and established a unique positioning in the evolving market|New products revenue of INR 3,526 Mn in FY 25-26, up 11.3% Y-o-Y, from intelligent industry-specific solutions across AI automation and omnichannel customer experience

risks.note: BRSR material-issues table flags that processing data exposes the Company to privacy breach claims, and that regulators such as TRAI define the rules for CPaaS players so changes to regulatory requirements could affect business potential; negative implication includes claims under privacy laws and the cost of hiring privacy professionals across jurisdictions. Mitigated via privacy policy, employee training, a compliance programme and audits.

Increasing cyber threats can compromise data and operations, with potential financial loss from data breaches and recovery costs; mitigated by advanced cybersecurity tooling, regular security audits and employee training.

Any downtime can result in poor customer experience and potential customer loss; mitigated with business continuity plans, regular drills and testing, and backup systems. Platform reliability is separately identified as the source of differentiation through high service delivery, requiring infrastructure strengthening, redundancy and continuous monitoring.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption across MNOs and infrastructure vendors
risks.note: Global events can disrupt the supply chain; any disruption in telecom partner operations or hardware vendors affects the ability to deliver quality services, causing delays and increased costs. Mitigated by diversifying the supplier pool and the network of operator connects.

Rapid technology change can render current systems obsolete, driving increased investment in technology updates; mitigated by regular tech refresh, R&D investment and staying ahead of industry developments.
New regulations can impose additional compliance requirements and costs, and inadvertent violation can create liability; mitigated by tracking regulatory changes and adjusting compliance programmes.

risks.risk: Talent retention in a niche skill pool
risks.note: Flagged as both opportunity and risk: revenue depends on a cutting-edge technology talent pool, and the Company may lose in talent retention if the millennial talent pool is not offered satisfactory career programmes and industry-competitive workplace facilities. Mitigation is talent re-skilling and attrition management.

one-line thesis: Route Mobile has structurally reset its business by exiting low-margin ILD volumes, driving FY26 gross profit above INR 1,000 cr despite a 3.7% revenue decline, while leveraging Proximus Global synergies to pivot toward high-margin Network APIs and AI-driven engagement. The strategic shift from pure connectivity to an intelligence layer positions the firm for mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth with expanding EBITDA margins (~12%) in FY27.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 4,408 cr FY26 (-3.7% YoY), Q4 INR 1,131 cr (+2.2% QoQ); EBITDA: INR 526 cr FY26 (+0.4% YoY), Margin 11.9% (vs 11.5% prior); PAT (Adj): INR 376 cr FY26 (+6.7% YoY), Q4 INR 114 cr (+34.6% YoY); Order Book: Undisclosed specific value but 'strong pipeline' for Firewall/APIs; Net Debt: Net Cash ~INR 1,400 cr. One-offs: FX gains and lower tax rate boosted Q4 PAT; Accounting distortion: Revenue compression due to mix shift (high-value ILD to lower-ARPU domestic) despite stable transaction volumes.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Mid-to-high single digits for FY27; EBITDA Margin: ~12%; Order Inflow: Strong pipeline for MNO Firewall & Network APIs; Capex: Disciplined, focused on capability-led M&A rather than heavy infrastructure.
order book & pipeline: Pipeline described as 'strong' for AI-driven A2P SMS/Voice firewall solutions and Network API deployments (e.g., Claro deal live); specific monetary value not quantified but cited as key future revenue driver alongside cross-sell with BICS/Telesign.
segment / subsidiary detail: Legacy A2P SMS (ILD) declined structurally but stabilized in Q4; now ~25-33% of revenue mix. New Products (RCS/WhatsApp/Omnichannel) grew 43% CAGR (FY22-26) but slowed to 11% YoY in FY26, constituting ~8% of revenue. MNO Solutions (Firewall/Network APIs) excluded from 'New Products' metric, growing fast with record revenue in Firewall, driven by operator fraud prevention needs.
growth verticals / optionality: Cross-sell into 3,100+ existing single-channel clients; Geographic expansion into Mexico/Philippines; US market entry via Telesign; 'India as Innovation Hub' model (e.g., Aakash Education proof point) scaled globally via Proximus; Bolt-on M&A for AI capabilities.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin expanded to 22.9% FY26 (from 20.8%) and 23.3% in Q4 due to exit of low-margin ILD and domestic mix shift. EBITDA margin improved to 11.9% driven by operating leverage and cost initiatives; OPEX constrained mainly to wage indexation.
capex / expansion: Strategy favors 'build vs buy' framework with preference for targeted, capability-led M&A (conversational AI/CPaaS adjacent) to compress 2-3 year build cycles into 12-18 months; no heavy greenfield capex highlighted.
capital allocation: Dividend increased 50% from INR 11 to INR 16.5 per share (sustainable quarterly payout); excess cash returned to shareholders while retaining flexibility for value-accretive bolt-on acquisitions.
risks & watch-items: Continued secular decline in ILD A2P SMS volumes; Slow adoption rate of new channels (RCS/WhatsApp) relative to competitor pace; Integration complexity of Proximus group synergies; Macro pressure on enterprise discretionary spend.
management quality / tone: Candid on past headwinds (AIT cleanup, ILD decline) but highly confident in structural reset; Emphasis on 'live program' execution rather than theoretical strategy; Disciplined capital allocator focused on quality of earnings over sheer scale.
non-obvious takeaways: Network API revenue (Silent Verification, SIM swap) is currently booked under legacy SMS segment, masking the true growth rate of the 'New Product' transition; The 'India as Innovation Hub' allows for rapid prototyping (e.g., Aakash deal in months) that is then distributed globally via Proximus, a unique arbitrage not available to standalone peers.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.
